claim: Recent neural and differentiable representations have changed this design space by treating mapping as a joint problem of geometry estimation, appearance modeling, and camera pose refinement.
context: Simultaneous localization and mapping is a core capability for autonomous robots operating in previously unseen environments. For many years, dense SLAM systems have mainly represented the world with point clouds, surfels, voxel grids, signed distance fields, or mesh-based maps. These geometric maps are useful for localization and obstacle avoidance, but they do not directly optimize the photorealistic appearance of a scene.
gold_papers: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
acceptable_papers: iMAP: Implicit Mapping and Positioning in Real-Time
forbidden_papers: pure geometric SLAM paper without neural/differentiable representation
3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM paper that only mentions NeRF in related work
notes: Tests whether claim understanding separates SLAM background from neural/differentiable representation mechanism.

claim: Existing 3DGS-SLAM systems generally depend on repeated photometric optimization and careful keyframe management to maintain map quality.
context: 3D Gaussian Splatting has become an attractive representation for dense visual SLAM because it supports photorealistic rendering and explicit scene primitives.
gold_papers: GS-SLAM: Dense Visual SLAM with 3D Gaussian Splatting
Gaussian-SLAM: Photo-realistic Dense SLAM with Gaussian Splatting
